text:
maya: quick note — I repro'd a latency spike on prod yesterday around 22:14 UTC. looks correlated with high prefix-hit ratio + continuous-batcher enabled on pool-gamma. attaching quick trace + notes.

samir: can you paste the trace link? was this during an autoscale event?

maya: https://internal.perf/trace/1715001234 flame shows long wait in packer while KV hits arriving. not an autoscale. spike ~120ms p95 -> 280ms p95 for short seqs.

jon: interesting. could be packer waiting for hit-prefill to finish and holding token budget. did we hit the token_budget_floor recently?

maya: looks like budget floor at 8 tokens, batcher was trying to maintain 64 token budget per batch but many items were 2-token continuation hits, so packer stalls to fill virtual length. result: queue grows and kernel selection flips to small-matmul path triggering overhead.

lee: can you share the exact batching config?

maya: here —
```
batching: {
  max_batch_size: 64,
  token_budget_target: 64,
  token_budget_floor: 8,
  wait_ms: 5,
  kv_cache_aware: true,
}
```

samir: a couple thoughts: (1) when kv_cache_aware=true we should use adjusted virtual_length = max(seq_len, hit_prefix_len_estimate) not raw seq_len for budget calc. (2) we may need a hit-dominance path that lowers target budget when hit_ratio > 0.7

jon: +1. Also kernel selection seems to mis-predict because estimated matmul size uses aggregated virtual length. If most are hits then kv kernel is cheap but we still pick heavy GEMM path because of worst-case. leads to per-request kernel warmup cost.

perfbot: perf snapshot 1715001234: avg_batch_size=12, avg_tokens_per_req=6.2, hit_ratio=0.72, p95_latency=280ms, packer_wait_ms=18.

maya: repro script in #eng-runtime/artifacts: ./repro/prefill_spillover.sh — run with --seed 42. It simulates 70% prefix hits small tail gen.

lee: propose two quick experiments: A) lower token_budget_target to 24 when hit_ratio > 0.6, B) add token_budget_ceiling and token_budget_decay for hit streams to avoid packer waiting for virtual length fill. Which do we try first?

samir: try A first — should be low-risk and testable via canary. set canary to 5% on pool-gamma. Also enable extra logging: packer.decision_trace.

jon: for canary, add kernel-selection telemetry too (chosen_kernel, est_virtual_len, batch_real_len). we need to see mis-select patterns.

maya: I'll push a canary PR today: r/1715001250 and enable perf logging. will run the repro after deploy.

samir: if A doesn't drop p95 to baseline, then B + quick fix in kernel selector to bias toward lightweight matmul when hit_ratio_high.

lee: also consider adding a short-circuit: when N consecutive batches were dominated by prefix hits, switch to "hit-mode" where packer uses smaller budget and batching timeout=1ms. cheap fallback, reduces backlog.

maya: noted. i'll run A and report results. thanks all. :thumbsup:

perfbot: scheduled job: run repro x10 at 1715001300, results will post in thread.
